identity.title: A Causal Decomposition Approach for Fair Contextual Multi-Armed Bandits

problem.claim: The paper studies counterfactual direct, indirect, and spurious effects as fairness measures for sequential decision-making, then formulates an online causally fair learning problem with multiple long-term constraints.

contributions.claim: A causal decomposition framework using counterfactual direct, indirect, and spurious effects to quantify fairness in contextual bandits.

Sublinear regret and constraint-violation bounds for non-parametric contextual and parametric logistic bandits under roundwise, initially unknown counterfactual-fairness constraints, without Slater’s condition.
For logistic bandits, an online mirror-descent estimator gives an algorithm with reported O(1) per-round time complexity.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report sublinear regret and violation bounds in both bandit settings without Slater’s condition.
The authors report O(1) per-round time complexity for their logistic-bandit method using an online mirror-descent estimator.

narrative_sequence.summary: Counterfactual reasoning is introduced as relevant to explanation, credit assignment, blame, and responsibility.
The project defines direct, indirect, and spurious counterfactual effects for fairness quantification in sequential decisions.
These measures support an online causally fair learning problem with multiple long-term constraints in two contextual-bandit settings.
The authors report sublinear regret and violation bounds without Slater’s condition, plus O(1) per-round logistic-bandit computation.

source_observation.claim: The abstract decomposes fairness into direct, indirect, and spurious counterfactual effects, then uses those measures as constraints in an online learning formulation.

lessons.interpretation: A multi-part construct can become operational when each component is explicitly connected to a controllable constraint.
lessons.application: When proposing a fairness framework, define distinct causal components and map each to the optimization constraints they induce.
lessons.exception: This move is unsuitable when the application lacks an interpretable causal structure or cannot support the required counterfactual quantities.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the formal definitions of the three effects, the constraint-violation metric, or the exact regret and violation rates.
It does not report experimental settings, numerical comparisons, or conditions underlying the O(1) complexity claim.
